method: Focused, bounded, AI-assisted desk review; not a systematic review or formal independent GRADE/AMSTAR assessment.

sources.title: American College of Sports Medicine Position Stand. Resistance Training Prescription for Muscle Function, Hypertrophy, and Physical Performance in Healthy Adults: An Overview of Reviews.
sources.authors: Currier BS, D'Souza AC, Singh MAF, Lowisz CV, Rawson ES, Schoenfeld BJ, Smith-Ryan AE, Steen JP, Thomas GA, Triplett NT, Washington TA, Werner TJ, Phillips SM.
sources.selection_reason: Current professional guidance; primary synthesis anchor
sources.population_and_design_scope: Healthy adults >=18; interventions >=6 weeks; most evidence in inexperienced trainees.
sources.appraisal: 137 reviews; search through October 2024; overlap assessed for strength but not all outcomes; variable study quality; source quality percentages are not individual success probabilities.
sources.inspected_locators: Methods: Eligibility Criteria; Methodological Quality Assessment and Evidence Synthesis; Overlap of Papers; Results: Tables 4 and 6; Discussion paragraphs on specificity, dose, failure, and limitations.

sources.title: Resistance training prescription for muscle strength and hypertrophy in healthy adults: a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Currier BS, Mcleod JC, Banfield L, Beyene J, Welton NJ, D'Souza AC, Keogh JAJ, Lin L, Coletta G, Yang A, Colenso-Semple L, Lau KJ, Verboom A, Phillips SM.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Healthy adults; athletes, military participants, chronic disease, and unsupervised interventions excluded.
sources.appraisal: Strength network 178 studies/5097 participants; hypertrophy 119/3364. Broad load/set/frequency bins; mainly some-concern/high-bias trials; many between-prescription intervals include zero, which does not establish equivalence.
sources.inspected_locators: Methods: Eligibility criteria; Condition coding framework; Results: Comparing RTxs; Discussion; Limitations.

sources.title: The Resistance Training Dose Response: Meta-Regressions Exploring the Effects of Weekly Volume and Frequency on Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains.
sources.authors: Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Robinson ZP, Hinson SR, Zourdos MC.
sources.selection_reason: Newer dose-response analysis after the ACSM search cutoff
sources.population_and_design_scope: 67 studies/2058 participants; mostly young adults and men, as reported in the abstract.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; exploratory multilevel meta-regression and model-dependent indirect-set accounting. Fractional 0.5 weighting is an analytic convention, not a biological conversion for every exercise or client.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: Methods; Results; Conclusions.
sources.date_note: Preserve first-publication date separately from bibliographic issue year.

sources.title: Dose-response relationship between weekly resistance training volume and increases in muscle mass: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Ogborn D, Krieger JW.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 15 studies/34 treatment groups of resistance-training interventions.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; older evidence also represented in newer reviews; do not extrapolate a per-set average into a linear individual growth formula. A linked published comment exists (S26); its text was not accessible.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract; Europe PMC commentCorrectionList.

sources.title: Effects of resistance training performed to repetition failure or non-failure on muscular strength and hypertrophy: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Grgic J, Schoenfeld BJ, Orazem J, Sabol F.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Young adults; strength 15 studies/394 participants, hypertrophy 7 studies/219; interventions 6-14 weeks.
sources.appraisal: Wide hypertrophy interval; differing definitions/loads/volume; trained subgroup hypertrophy relied on only two studies. Not proof of equivalence or a precise RIR optimum.
sources.inspected_locators: Results: Study characteristics; Discussion: Muscle hypertrophy; Generalizability of the results; Methodological quality and limitations.

sources.title: Exploring the Dose-Response Relationship Between Estimated Resistance Training Proximity to Failure, Strength Gain, and Muscle Hypertrophy: A Series of Meta-Regressions.
sources.authors: Robinson ZP, Pelland JC, Remmert JF, Refalo MC, Jukic I, Steele J, Zourdos MC.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Strength/hypertrophy training studies analyzed using estimated RIR.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; RIR reconstructed from intervention descriptions, exploratory regressions, modest fit. Supports possible outcome-specific association, not a causal numeric target for individuals.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: Objective; Results; Conclusions.

sources.title: Influence of Resistance Training Proximity-to-Failure on Skeletal Muscle Hypertrophy: A Systematic Review with Meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Refalo MC, Helms ER, Trexler ET, Hamilton DL, Fyfe JJ.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 15 studies of healthy adult hypertrophy outcomes.
sources.appraisal: Failure definitions vary; pooled trivial set-failure advantage is sensitive to assumed pre/post correlation; momentary-failure subgroup interval includes zero. Actual RIR not consistently known.
sources.inspected_locators: Results: Meta-analysis Results; Discussion: Practical Application of Key Findings; Limitations; Conclusions.

sources.title: Effect of free-weight vs. machine-based strength training on maximal strength, hypertrophy and jump performance - a systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Haugen ME, Vårvik FT, Larsen S, Haugen AS, van den Tillaar R, Bjørnsen T.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Adults 18-60 without chronic disease/injury; 13 studies, typically 6-12 weeks; no competitive athletes.
sources.appraisal: Sparse hypertrophy evidence, heterogeneous measurement and protocols; no equivalence trial. Reported overall participant total and sex subtotals do not reconcile; do not invent a corrected total.
sources.inspected_locators: Methods: Inclusion criteria; Results: Characteristics of the included studies; The effect of free-weight- versus machine-based training on hypertrophy; Weaknesses.

sources.title: Give it a rest: a systematic review with Bayesian meta-analysis on the effect of inter-set rest interval duration on muscle hypertrophy.
sources.authors: Singer A, Wolf M, Generoso L, Arias E, Delcastillo K, Echevarria E, Martinez A, Androulakis Korakakis P, Refalo MC, Swinton PA, Schoenfeld BJ.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 9 studies, 19 measurements; mostly young/untrained participants; 5-10 weeks.
sources.appraisal: Small uncertain between-group effects; limb-focused evidence and mixed volume protocols; no precise universal optimum or upper bound at 90 seconds.
sources.inspected_locators: Results: Study characteristics; Meta-analysis of controlled effect sizes; Discussion: Limitations; Conclusion.

sources.title: What influence does resistance exercise order have on muscular strength gains and muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Nunes JP, Grgic J, Cunha PM, Ribeiro AS, Schoenfeld BJ, de Salles BF, Cyrino ES.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 11 studies of resistance exercise order and strength/hypertrophy.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; order effects are task-specific. No detectable hypertrophy effect does not prove all sequencing schemes equivalent.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: Methods and results; concluding sentences.

sources.title: Does Varying Resistance Exercises Promote Superior Muscle Hypertrophy and Strength Gains? A Systematic Review.
sources.authors: Kassiano W, Nunes JP, Costa B, Ribeiro AS, Schoenfeld BJ, Cyrino ES.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 8 studies, 241 participants, all young men, per abstract.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; narrow population and heterogeneous systematic/random variation. Does not establish a universal exercise-rotation schedule or a need for constant novelty.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: study selection, population, and conclusions.

sources.title: Superset Versus Traditional Resistance Training Prescriptions: A Systematic Review and Meta-analysis Exploring Acute and Chronic Effects on Mechanical, Metabolic, and Perceptual Variables.
sources.authors: Zhang X, Weakley J, Li H, Li Z, García-Ramos A.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 19 studies/313 participants; 16 acute-only and 3 chronic studies; mostly young trained men, with at least one adolescent sample.
sources.appraisal: Strength chronic estimate uses 3 studies; hypertrophy only 2; wide intervals and protocol heterogeneity. Source conclusions about similar adaptations are not equivalence evidence and are indirect for arbitrary 3-5 exercise circuits.
sources.inspected_locators: Results: Study Characteristics; Risk of Bias Assessment; Meta-analysis: Acute Effects and Chronic Variables; Discussion: Limitations; Table 5.

sources.title: Interpreting Signal Amplitudes in Surface Electromyography Studies in Sport and Rehabilitation Sciences.
sources.authors: Vigotsky AD, Halperin I, Lehman GJ, Trajano GS, Vieira TM.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Narrative methodological review of surface EMG in sport/rehabilitation.
sources.appraisal: Not an intervention meta-analysis; describes why raw amplitudes are not a validated general surrogate for long-term strength/hypertrophy. Preserve muscle, electrode, normalization, task, and measurement context.
sources.inspected_locators: What conclusions cannot be drawn from sEMG studies?: Longitudinal outcomes; Interim summary; Conclusions.
sources.date_note: Europe PMC pubYear is 2017 (volume); firstPublicationDate and article XML are 2018-01-04. Cite as Vigotsky et al. 2018 with both dates preserved.

sources.title: Novel Resistance Training-Specific Rating of Perceived Exertion Scale Measuring Repetitions in Reserve.
sources.authors: Zourdos MC, Klemp A, Dolan C, Quiles JM, Schau KA, Jo E, Helms E, Esgro B, Duncan S, Garcia Merino S, Blanco R.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 29 experienced/novice squatters; primary study.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; exercise-specific small study. Do not convert its scale validation into a universal exact load/RIR prediction or an energy-score prescription.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: sample, protocol, RPE/RIR mapping, and conclusions.

sources.title: Accuracy in Predicting Repetitions to Task Failure in Resistance Exercise: A Scoping Review and Exploratory Meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Halperin I, Malleron T, Har-Nir I, Androulakis-Korakakis P, Wolf M, Fisher J, Steele J.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Scoping review; 12 studies/414 participants in exploratory meta-analysis.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; very high heterogeneity; average underprediction is not a correction to apply to every person. Training background did not reliably remove prediction error.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: Search and inclusion; Results; Conclusions.

sources.title: Autoregulated resistance training for maximal strength enhancement: A systematic review and network meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Zijing Huang, Sun J, Li D, Chen C, Wang D.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Trained/sport populations including ages 10-30; squat/bench outcomes; not exclusively adults.
sources.appraisal: Retrieved text reports 438 participants in characteristics vs 428 in discussion, and malformed CI endpoints in NMA prose. Sparse RPE/APRE comparisons, intervals crossing zero, and ranks do not justify the broad superiority conclusion. Do not silently repair numbers or implement an automatic policy from rankings.
sources.inspected_locators: Methods: Study selection and eligibility criteria; Results: Characteristics of the included studies; NMA of back squat 1RM; NMA of bench press 1RM; Discussion.

sources.title: Does Muscle Length Influence Regional Hypertrophy? A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
sources.authors: Varovic D, Wolf M, Schoenfeld BJ, Steele J, Grgic J, Mikulic P.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 12 studies in young adults, per abstract.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; modest average contrast between longer/shorter conditions (21.8% mean muscle length); near-zero/small estimates do not settle all muscles, loading profiles, or fascicle adaptations.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: methods, regional effect estimates, and caution about contrast size.

sources.title: Effects of range of motion on muscle development during resistance training interventions: A systematic review.
sources.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 6 studies/135 participants, 127 men and 8 women; mostly untrained.
sources.appraisal: Predominantly lower-body, limited/conflicting upper-body evidence and no trunk studies in that review. Older than emerging long-length work; do not generalize full-ROM superiority to every muscle/outcome.
sources.inspected_locators: Results; Discussion; Conclusion.

sources.title: Does longer-muscle length resistance training cause greater longitudinal growth in humans? A systematic review.
sources.authors: Wolf M, Korakakis PA, Roberts MD, Plotkin DL, Franchi MV, Contreras B, Henselmans M, Larsen S, Schoenfeld BJ.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 8 studies/120 adults; predominantly vastus lateralis and untrained participants.
sources.appraisal: Fascicle length is mostly estimated by linear extrapolation; no direct serial sarcomere counts, mixed study quality and uncontrolled work. Architecture outcome differs from regional size in S17.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract; Discussion; Conclusion.
sources.date_note: Preserve first-publication date separately from bibliographic issue year.

sources.title: What is resistance exercise? A review of current uses and potential ways forward.
sources.authors: Lohmann LH, Afonso J, Behm DG, Siegel SD, Keiner M, Wirth K, Blazevich AJ, Helms ER, Spence AJ, Warneke K.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Narrative/conceptual review of resistance-exercise definitions.
sources.appraisal: A proposed definition rather than an accepted consensus or tested outcome model; useful for recording execution/effort context, not for declaring a validated ontology or exercise threshold.
sources.inspected_locators: Definitional inconsistencies; Proposing a new framework with remaining gaps.

sources.title: The interplay between muscle length, range of motion, and exercise selection: a review.
sources.authors: Pedrosa GF, Pereira MR, Kassiano W.
sources.selection_reason: Context for length, ROM, and resistance profile
sources.population_and_design_scope: Unstructured narrative review of longitudinal muscle-length/ROM/exercise studies.
sources.appraisal: No systematic pooled effect; its mechanistic interpretation should not override bounded systematic-review results or become a universal optimal-length rule.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract; Conclusions; exercise/ROM comparisons in the article.

sources.title: How many times per week should a muscle be trained to maximize muscle hypertrophy? A systematic review and meta-analysis of studies examining the effects of resistance training frequency.
sources.authors: Schoenfeld BJ, Grgic J, Krieger J.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 25 studies of training frequency and hypertrophy, per abstract.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; older and overlapping with later syntheses; frequency must be interpreted alongside total weekly volume, not as an independent guaranteed benefit.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: volume-equated and non-volume-equated analyses; conclusion.

sources.title: Effects of resistance training performed to repetition non-failure on exercise performance in healthy adults: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
sources.authors: Wu S, Xie L, Zhao Z, Zheng X, Yin X, Hou J, Zhou K, Tang P.
sources.selection_reason: Newer failure comparison after the ACSM search cutoff
sources.population_and_design_scope: 20 studies/556 participants, mean ages 19.0-67.6; mixes training backgrounds.
sources.appraisal: Definitions, volume, and termination methods differ. Small non-failure dynamic-strength advantage does not establish universal superiority; no significant differences for other outcomes are not proof of equivalence.
sources.inspected_locators: Results: Participant characteristics; Training protocol; GRADE assessment; Discussion: Limitations; Conclusions.

sources.title: Greater Hamstrings Muscle Hypertrophy but Similar Damage Protection after Training at Long versus Short Muscle Lengths.
sources.authors: Maeo S, Huang M, Wu Y, Sakurai H, Kusagawa Y, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 20 healthy adults in within-participant seated-vs-prone leg-curl training; 12 weeks.
sources.appraisal: One small exercise-specific trial with MRI volume measures; no universal ranking, individualized growth forecast, transferable load ratio, or clinical injury prevention effect.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: Methods and Results, part 1; Discussion: Limitations.

sources.title: Triceps brachii hypertrophy is substantially greater after elbow extension training performed in the overhead versus neutral arm position.
sources.authors: Maeo S, Wu Y, Huang M, Sakurai H, Kusagawa Y, Sugiyama T, Kanehisa H, Isaka T.
sources.population_and_design_scope: 21 adults; within-participant overhead-vs-neutral cable elbow extensions; 12 weeks.
sources.appraisal: Abstract only; one small study and specific apparatus/ROM/progression. Do not generalize the protocol progression or infer lower injury risk from lower lifted kilograms.
sources.inspected_locators: Abstract: protocol, MRI-measured muscle volume results, and limitations of scope.

sources.title: Reliability of meta-analyses to evaluate resistance training programmes.
sources.authors: Arruda A, Souza D, Steele J, Fisher J, Giessing J, Gentil P.
sources.population_and_design_scope: Metadata-only comment on S04.
sources.appraisal: No abstract or full text inspected; content not appraised. A Comment on/in link is not an erratum or retraction; the critique is not claimed to be resolved.
sources.inspected_locators: Europe PMC bibliographic record and commentCorrectionList only.

integrity_note: Hashes identify the received Europe PMC search-response bytes and open full-text XML at retrieval time. Full texts/abstracts remain in temporary research storage and are not redistributed here.
